## Dimension-by-Dimension Assessment

### 1. CLI/Script Execution — Windmill Stronger

Windmill treats Bash as a first-class language with native argument passing,
stdout capture, and result.json structured output [5]. n8n requires the
Execute Command node which is more limited. Windmill also supports Docker
container execution via annotations [33]. For a PA that runs CLI tools,
this is a significant advantage.

### 2. Credential Isolation — Windmill Stronger

Both encrypt credentials, but Windmill's `$var:` resolution model and
pre-scoped webhook tokens provide cleaner separation between the triggering
agent and the credentials [6][9]. Windmill's audit logging of secret access
adds visibility (EE) [6].

### 3. Self-Hosting Resources — n8n Stronger

n8n runs in a single container at ~100 MB idle [n8n research]. Windmill
requires server + workers + PostgreSQL with ~2-4 GB minimum [4][34]. For
a personal workstation running alongside dev tools, n8n has a smaller
footprint.

### 4. API Completeness — Windmill Stronger

Windmill publishes a full OpenAPI spec with client libraries and MCP
integration [13][14]. n8n has a REST API but it's less comprehensively
documented.

### 5. Webhook Flexibility — Windmill Stronger

Windmill offers 7 authentication options for HTTP routes including HMAC
signature verification with Stripe/GitHub presets [10]. n8n webhooks are
simpler with fewer auth options.

### 6. AI/LLM Integration — n8n Stronger

n8n has 70+ LangChain nodes, 12+ vector stores, native RAG, and deep AI
ecosystem integration [n8n research]. Windmill has functional but simpler
AI agent steps [15]. However, for the PA use case where the engine runs
deterministic pipelines, this dimension matters less.

### 7. Community & Ecosystem — n8n Stronger

n8n has 150K+ stars, 5,800+ community nodes, $40M revenue, and a $2.5B
valuation [n8n research]. Windmill has 16K stars, 48 contributors, and
$2.7M revenue [2][25]. n8n's ecosystem is an order of magnitude larger.

### 8. License — Windmill Stronger

Windmill's AGPL-3.0 is OSI-approved [40]. n8n's Sustainable Use License
is not OSI-compliant and restricts commercial use [n8n research]. For
personal use neither matters, but AGPL-3.0 is a more standard open-source
license.

### 9. Performance — Windmill Stronger (Claimed)

"13x faster than Airflow" (claimed), Rust backend. Specific step latency
not published [1].
n8n is Node.js-based with no published overhead numbers. However, for a
personal PA running a few workflows, performance differences are
negligible.

### 10. Scheduling — Roughly Equal

Both support cron scheduling. Windmill uses an extended syntax (L, #, W
modifiers) [8]. n8n uses standard cron [n8n research]. Both adequate for
the use case.

## Limitations and Gaps (Windmill)

### Resource Footprint
Multi-component architecture (server + workers + PostgreSQL) requires more
RAM than single-container alternatives. Estimated 2-4 GB minimum vs ~100 MB
for n8n [4][34].

### Ecosystem Size
Far fewer pre-built integrations compared to n8n (400+ nodes) or Zapier
(7,000+). Windmill's philosophy is "write a script" rather than "pick a
node" [3].

### Enterprise Feature Gating
Several useful features are Enterprise-only [16]:
- Audit logs (full, not redacted)
- Git sync
- Content search / full-text search
- Worker group management UI
- Concurrency limits
- SAML/SCIM
- Schedule error handlers

### Podman Support
Not documented or tested. Requires Docker socket for container-based script
execution [4][5][33].

### Custom Tool Installation
CLI tools (gws, gh, etc.) must be installed in worker containers or accessed
via Docker annotation. No built-in system package declaration [5].

### Maturity
Younger project (2022 vs n8n 2019), smaller team (18 vs 67), smaller
community. Very high release velocity (multiple per day) may indicate
rapid iteration but also potential instability [2].

### Pricing Concerns for Self-Hosted
Enterprise self-hosted pricing charges per compute unit ($50/worker/month)
on user-owned infrastructure, which generated community criticism [17][19].
Community Edition is free and unlimited for self-hosted, so this only
affects users needing EE features.

## When Windmill Beats n8n (for PA Use Case)

1. Native Bash execution is stronger than n8n's Execute Command node
2. Better credential isolation model (pre-scoped tokens, $var: resolution)
3. MCP server enables direct PA-to-engine interaction
4. Full REST API with OpenAPI spec and client libraries
5. More webhook authentication options
6. OSI-compliant license

## When n8n Beats Windmill (for PA Use Case)

1. Lower resource footprint (~100 MB vs ~2-4 GB)
2. Larger community and ecosystem (10x stars, 5,800+ community nodes)
3. Deeper AI/LLM integration (70+ nodes vs basic agent steps)
4. More mature project with larger team
5. Simpler deployment (single container possible)
6. Already evaluated hands-on

## Gaps and Limitations (This Analysis)

- Quantitative performance benchmarks across platforms not available
- Hosting cost estimates from third-party blog posts, not rigorous benchmarks
- n8n data from prior research (March 2026); may have changed
- Windmill's rapid release cadence means features may have changed since
  documentation was last updated
